Messages.Author: Mike Mayer
Messages.Body:
Concerning the change of card backs...

Well, I have almost a complete set. I have dozens of the commons. I
need no more. But, what if I like the idea of an expansion and its
cards are different. So I buy a couple packs to pick up Necromancy to
add to my selection of skills. So, if I add Necromancy to one
of my decks, they will all be the new backs. Thus, all one skill is
in one card back. Am I spiking my deck, well yes. Is it my fault, no.
But, unless I buy all new cards, my deck would inadvertantly be spiked.
So who's problem is this? WoTC, cause I ain't buying any more cards.

Mike

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Joseph Cochran <js...@discus.ise.vt.edu> wrote:
>>Well, sort of. WotC sold 180 million cards, but the game is still
>>readily availble at the retail level.
> And this is bad? Personally, the availability of the game is a
>very nice thing. And the retailers in our area are glad to have a game
>that people can get.

It's not bad, it just seemed like you were claiming Jyhad was totally
sold out, which is not quite true, so I corrected. If that's not what
you were claiming, then never mind. :)

>>There is no second print run of Jyhad, unless you call V:TES a second
>>print run of Jyhad, which strikes me as a little dicey.
> Yes, I consider V:tES a second print run, considering that
>Magic's changes of cards were considered to be the same game.
> Unless, of course, you're changing the game so much that you
>consider it to be a different game, which strikes *me* as duplicitous.

Well, the game is essentially a rerelease of Jyhad under a new name and
a somewhat different presentation. For example, there are material differences
in the cards, such as the different card backs, and the different card borders
for the various types of minion cards. So it just seems weird to talk about
it as a strict reprinting of Jyhad. Maybe it's just me.

> So the company took a product which bombed, and is sinking more
>money into it to try again with new marketing? Is this what you're
>saying? Best of luck...

I wouldn't say Jyhad bombed, but it's not selling as well as it could, and
the old presentation of the game is a major reason why it's not selling to
certain market segments. Hence the new marketing approach.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3o6mdj$j...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>,

Thomas R Wylie <aa...@cats.ucsc.edu> wrote:
>Joseph Cochran <js...@discus.ise.vt.edu> wrote:

>>>There is no second print run of Jyhad, unless you call V:TES a second
>>>print run of Jyhad, which strikes me as a little dicey.
>> Yes, I consider V:tES a second print run, considering that
>>Magic's changes of cards were considered to be the same game.
>> Unless, of course, you're changing the game so much that you
>>consider it to be a different game, which strikes *me* as duplicitous.
>
>Well, the game is essentially a rerelease of Jyhad under a new name and
>a somewhat different presentation. For example, there are material differences
>in the cards, such as the different card backs, and the different card borders
>for the various types of minion cards. So it just seems weird to talk about
>it as a strict reprinting of Jyhad. Maybe it's just me.

You can't have it both ways. Either it *is* the same game
reprinted or it *isn't*. You change the game, or you don't. You (the
company) have gone to great lengths to say that the game is the same,
that it's only the cosmetics that will change. If this is true, then
the game is a reprinting of Jyhad. If not, it is a new game. It's as
simple as that.

>I wouldn't say Jyhad bombed, but it's not selling as well as it could, and
>the old presentation of the game is a major reason why it's not selling to
>certain market segments. Hence the new marketing approach.

The post you were corroborating with your statements was a post
that said that Jyhad bombed. Thus, the implication you gave was that
you agreed that Jyhad bombed. Personally, from all reports I've had
through the net and through friends who are retailers, the game sold
reasonably well and was a solid game compared to other products they
sell. It wasn't Magic, but it was a solid game sales-wise. Nobody took
a bath from it. I wish you the best of luck with the new marketing, but
I seriously wonder how the change will affect your installed customer
base. We can see what the net thinks, but you're not changing it for
us, so I'll be interested to see what kind of a barometer we are for the
larger market that you intend to capture.


